Producing Fieldwork Resources for Survey Data Collection

Source: vignettes/fieldwork-survey-resources.Rmd
fieldwork-survey-resources.Rmd

Overview

Household surveys, agricultural censuses, and ground-truth campaigns rely on high-resolution satellite imagery to delineate Enumeration Areas (EAs), verify building footprints, and guide field enumerators to sampled structures.

vantorr provides a dedicated suite of fieldwork functions that turn Vantor / Maxar satellite basemaps and seamline metadata into ready-to-use survey resources:

  1. vantor_survey_grid(): Partition an Area of Interest (AOI) into square or hexagonal survey index cells labeled "A1", "A2", "B1", etc.
  2. vantor_vintage_report(): Audit the acquisition dates (acq_time), resolution (gsd), and sensor quality of Vantor basemap strips across each Enumeration Area to flag outdated imagery before deploying field teams.
  3. vantor_plus_code() & vantor_export_capi(): Enrich sample points with offline-capable Open Location Codes (Google Plus Codes), grid cell assignments (cell_id), and imagery acquisition dates (imagery_acq_date), and export platform-specific preload files:
    • CSV (.csv) & GeoJSON (.geojson) with odk_geopoint ("lat lon 0 0") for ODK Collect, KoboToolbox, and ArcGIS Survey123.
    • Tab-delimited (.tab) assignment preload tables (output_suso_tab) with <gps_var>__Latitude, <gps_var>__Longitude, and _target_area for World Bank Survey Solutions (or direct programmatic assignment creation via the SurveySolutionsAPIv2 R package).
  4. vantor_field_atlas(): Generate a multi-page printable PDF Field Atlas (Map Book) featuring an Overview Index sheet and zoomed-in Enumeration Area detail sheets with Vantor satellite imagery, scale bars, north arrows, and enumerator sign-off footers.
  5. vantor_offline_package() & vantor_write_tpk(): Bundle vector layers (.gpkg, zipped .shp), CAPI preload tables (.csv and Survey Solutions .tab), georeferenced Web Mercator basemaps (.tif), and multi-zoom Esri Tile Packages (.tpk / .tpkx and clean _tpk.zip upload archives) into a portable directory for offline tablet apps (World Bank Survey Solutions, QField, Mergin Maps, ArcGIS Field Maps). See vignette("survey-solutions-workflow", package = "vantorr") for the dedicated Survey Solutions & SurveySolutionsAPIv2 guide.

1. Generating an Alphanumeric Survey Index Grid

Start by defining your survey Area of Interest (using any sf, terra, or stars object, or a WGS84 bounding box) and partitioning it into a metric enumeration grid with vantor_survey_grid():

library(vantorr)
library(sf)
#> Linking to GEOS 3.12.1, GDAL 3.8.4, PROJ 9.4.0; sf_use_s2() is TRUE

# Define a 1.5 km x 1.5 km survey Area of Interest in WGS84 (EPSG:4326)
aoi <- st_bbox(
  c(xmin = -105.010, ymin = 39.730, xmax = -104.995, ymax = 39.742),
  crs = st_crs(4326)
)

# Generate a 500 m square survey grid with alphanumeric labels (A1, A2, B1, ...)
survey_grid <- vantor_survey_grid(
  aoi = aoi,
  cell_size = 500,
  shape = "square",
  verbose = FALSE
)

survey_grid[, c("cell_id", "row_idx", "col_idx", "centroid_lon", "centroid_lat", "area_m2")]
#> Simple feature collection with 16 features and 6 fields
#> Geometry type: POLYGON

You can also generate hexagonal tessellations for spatial cluster sampling by setting shape = "hexagonal":

hex_grid <- vantor_survey_grid(
  aoi = aoi,
  cell_size = 500,
  shape = "hexagonal",
  verbose = FALSE
)

2. Auditing Imagery Vintage Across Enumeration Areas

When using satellite imagery to list households or sample structures, survey managers need to know whether the mosaic over each Enumeration Area is recent or several years old.

vantor_vintage_report() intersects your survey_grid (or Enumeration Area polygons) with Vantor’s OGC WFS Seamlines metadata (vantor_get_seamlines()) and calculates per-cell vintage metrics, flagging any cells where the imagery is older than max_age_days (default 730 days / 2 years):

# In an online session with Vantor credentials, seamlines are fetched automatically:
# vintage_grid <- vantor_vintage_report(survey_grid, product = "VIVID_STANDARD_30")

# Offline demonstration using synthetic seamline polygons:
bb_mid <- -105.0025
strip_west <- st_bbox(c(xmin = -105.012, ymin = 39.728, xmax = bb_mid, ymax = 39.745), crs = st_crs(4326))
strip_east <- st_bbox(c(xmin = bb_mid, ymin = 39.728, xmax = -104.990, ymax = 39.745), crs = st_crs(4326))

mock_seamlines <- st_sf(
  acq_time = c("2025-08-14T17:45:00Z", "2021-03-20T18:10:00Z"),
  gsd = c(0.30, 0.31),
  ona = c(10.2, 18.5),
  sensor = c("WV03", "WV02"),
  catid = c("10400100AA11", "10300100BB22"),
  geometry = c(st_as_sfc(strip_west), st_as_sfc(strip_east))
)

vintage_grid <- vantor_vintage_report(
  aoi = survey_grid,
  seamlines = mock_seamlines,
  max_age_days = 730,
  reference_date = as.Date("2026-10-15"),
  verbose = FALSE
)

st_drop_geometry(vintage_grid)[, c(
  "cell_id", "n_strips", "earliest_acq_date", "latest_acq_date",
  "max_age_days", "sensors", "vintage_warning"
)]
#>    cell_id n_strips earliest_acq_date latest_acq_date max_age_days    sensors
#> 1       A1        1        2025-08-14      2025-08-14          427       WV03
#> 2       A2        2        2021-03-20      2025-08-14         2035 WV03, WV02
#> 3       A3        1        2021-03-20      2021-03-20         2035       WV02
#> 4       A4        1        2021-03-20      2021-03-20         2035       WV02

3. Preparing CAPI Sample Preloads & Offline Plus Codes

Once household or cluster sample points are selected within your Enumeration Areas, vantor_export_capi() enriches them with coordinates, ODK / Kobo geopoint strings, offline Google Plus Codes (vantor_plus_code()), one-click Google Maps navigation links, grid cell assignments (cell_id), and imagery acquisition dates (imagery_acq_date).

Because different CAPI platforms expect different preload schemas, vantor_export_capi() supports three simultaneous export targets:

  • output_csv & output_geojson: Standard CSV and GeoJSON files containing odk_geopoint ("lat lon 0 0") for pulldata() in ODK Collect, KoboToolbox, and ArcGIS Survey123.
  • output_suso_tab (suso_gps_var = "hh_gps"): A tab-delimited (.tab) assignment preload file formatted specifically for World Bank Survey Solutions Headquarters (Survey Setup -> Questionnaires -> Upload Assignments). It automatically splits coordinates into <suso_gps_var>__Latitude and <suso_gps_var>__Longitude so preloaded households appear as interactive pins on the Interviewer tablet’s Map Dashboard, sets _target_area from cell_id, and includes plus_code and imagery_acq_date for cover-page display.
# Create sample household locations across the AOI
sample_pts <- st_as_sf(
  data.frame(
    hh_id = c("HH-101", "HH-102", "HH-103", "HH-104"),
    head_name = c("Household A", "Household B", "Household C", "Household D"),
    lon = c(-105.008, -105.004, -105.001, -104.997),
    lat = c(39.739, 39.738, 39.734, 39.733)
  ),
  coords = c("lon", "lat"),
  crs = 4326
)

# Enrich samples and export to ODK CSV, GeoJSON, and Survey Solutions .tab
csv_file <- tempfile(pattern = "odk_preload_", fileext = ".csv")
geojson_file <- tempfile(pattern = "field_samples_", fileext = ".geojson")
suso_tab_file <- tempfile(pattern = "suso_preload_", fileext = ".tab")

capi_samples <- vantor_export_capi(
  samples = sample_pts,
  id_col = "hh_id",
  grid = vintage_grid,
  seamlines = mock_seamlines,
  output_csv = csv_file,
  output_geojson = geojson_file,
  output_suso_tab = suso_tab_file,
  suso_gps_var = "hh_gps",
  verbose = FALSE
)

st_drop_geometry(capi_samples)[, c(
  "sample_id", "cell_id", "plus_code",
  "hh_gps__Latitude", "hh_gps__Longitude",
  "imagery_acq_date", "imagery_sensor"
)]
#>   sample_id cell_id   plus_code hh_gps__Latitude hh_gps__Longitude
#> 1    HH-101      B1 85FPPXQR+JR           39.739          -105.008
#> 2    HH-102      B2 85FPPXQW+6C           39.738          -105.004
#> 3    HH-103      C3 85FPPXMX+JJ           39.734          -105.001
#> 4    HH-104      D3 85FQP2M3+66           39.733          -104.997
#>   imagery_acq_date imagery_sensor
#> 1       2025-08-14           WV03
#> 2       2025-08-14           WV03
#> 3       2021-03-20           WV02
#> 4       2021-03-20           WV02

Inspecting the generated Survey Solutions .tab file confirms that it contains the exact <gps_var>__Latitude, <gps_var>__Longitude, and _target_area columns required by Survey Solutions Headquarters:

read.delim(suso_tab_file, check.names = FALSE)[, c(
  "sample_id", "cell_id", "plus_code",
  "hh_gps__Latitude", "hh_gps__Longitude",
  "_target_area"
)]
#>   sample_id cell_id   plus_code hh_gps__Latitude hh_gps__Longitude _target_area
#> 1    HH-101      B1 85FPPXQR+JR           39.739          -105.008           B1
#> 2    HH-102      B2 85FPPXQW+6C           39.738          -105.004           B2
#> 3    HH-103      C3 85FPPXMX+JJ           39.734          -105.001           C3
#> 4    HH-104      D3 85FQP2M3+66           39.733          -104.997           D3

Enumerators can type the preloaded plus_code (e.g., 85FPPXQR+JR) from the interview cover page directly into Google Maps or OSM on a mobile tablet to get turn-by-turn routing to the sampled structure completely offline, then switch to the offline Vantor .tpk basemap for the final 100 meters.

4. Generating a Multi-Page Printable Field Atlas (PDF Map Book)

For paper back-up maps and field supervisor binders, vantor_field_atlas() generates a multi-page PDF Map Book containing:

  • Page 1 (Overview Index Sheet): Shows the entire AOI, all grid cell boundaries and labels (A1, A2, …), and all sample locations.
  • Pages 2..N (Detail Enumeration Sheets): One page per grid cell, zoomed in with a configurable buffer (buffer_m = 50), metric scale bar, north arrow, sample point labels, imagery vintage date, and a field notes sign-off line.
atlas_pdf <- tempfile(pattern = "vantor_atlas_", fileext = ".pdf")

vantor_field_atlas(
  grid = vintage_grid,
  points = capi_samples,
  output_file = atlas_pdf,
  title = "Denver Survey Enumeration Atlas",
  buffer_m = 50,
  fetch_basemap = FALSE, # Set fetch_basemap = TRUE when authenticated to embed Vantor RGB imagery
  verbose = FALSE
)

file.exists(atlas_pdf)
#> [1] TRUE

When authenticated with Vantor (vantor_has_auth()), simply set fetch_basemap = TRUE (or pass a pre-downloaded SpatRaster via raster = ...) to render the 30 cm or 15 cm Vantor Vivid RGB satellite basemap underneath every page of the PDF atlas:

vantor_field_atlas(
  grid = vintage_grid,
  points = capi_samples,
  output_file = "denver_field_atlas.pdf",
  fetch_basemap = TRUE,
  resolution = 0.3,
  product = "VIVID_STANDARD_30"
)

5. Packaging Offline Mobile GIS & Survey Solutions Bundles (vantor_offline_package() & vantor_write_tpk())

To deploy your survey grid, CAPI sample points, seamline vintage polygons, and georeferenced Vantor satellite imagery to mobile CAPI and GIS apps—including World Bank Survey Solutions (v24.09+ built on the ArcGIS Maps SDK for .NET v200.x), QField, Mergin Maps, and ArcGIS Field Maps—use vantor_offline_package() and vantor_write_tpk():

  • Esri Tile Packages (.tpk / .tpkx) and Clean Upload Archives (_tpk.zip): vantor_write_tpk() builds multi-zoom Web Mercator (EPSG:3857 / Esri WKID: 102100) tile pyramids in pure R without requiring proprietary ArcGIS software or ArcGIS Online credits. Setting zip_for_suso = TRUE also creates a <stem>_tpk.zip archive stripped of macOS __MACOSX/._* resource forks for direct upload to Survey Solutions Headquarters (Survey Setup -> Maps).
  • Zipped Esri Shapefiles (_shapes.zip): Setting create_shapefiles = TRUE exports Enumeration Area grid cells and sample points as EPSG:4326 Shapefiles (including a label attribute column for automatic feature labeling in Survey Solutions) zipped at the archive root.
  • Survey Solutions .tab Preload (_suso_preload.tab) & ODK .csv (_samples.csv): Automatically generated whenever samples is supplied.
  • Web Mercator GeoTIFFs (.tif): Any included raster basemap is automatically reprojected to EPSG:3857 so Survey Solutions’ Esri RasterLayer engine renders it accurately.
bundle <- vantor_offline_package(
  grid = vintage_grid,
  samples = capi_samples,
  seamlines = mock_seamlines,
  create_shapefiles = TRUE, # Zipped Shapefiles for Survey Solutions HQ
  fetch_basemap = FALSE,    # Set TRUE to download and include the GeoTIFF basemap
  package_name = "denver_survey_ea",
  verbose = FALSE
)

# Inspect the generated multi-layer GeoPackage, ODK CSV, Survey Solutions .tab, and Shapefile ZIP
bundle$layers
#> [1] "survey_grid"       "survey_samples"    "imagery_seamlines"
basename(c(bundle$gpkg_path, bundle$csv_path, bundle$suso_tab_path, bundle$shapefile_zip_path))
#> [1] "denver_survey_ea.gpkg"             "denver_survey_ea_samples.csv"     
#> [3] "denver_survey_ea_suso_preload.tab" "denver_survey_ea_shapes.zip"
st_layers(bundle$gpkg_path)
#> Driver: GPKG 
#> Available layers:
#>          layer_name geometry_type features fields crs_name
#> 1       survey_grid       Polygon       16     15   WGS 84
#> 2    survey_samples         Point        4     11   WGS 84
#> 3 imagery_seamlines       Polygon        2      5   WGS 84

To generate a standalone multi-zoom .tpk (and clean _tpk.zip upload archive) directly from Vantor WMS imagery or an existing terra::SpatRaster:

# Online: fetch zoom levels 15-17 directly from Vantor WMS into a .tpk + _tpk.zip
vantor_write_tpk(
  x = vintage_grid,
  output_file = "denver_ea_basemap.tpk",
  zoom = 15:17,
  product = "VIVID_STANDARD_30",
  zip_for_suso = TRUE
)

For a step-by-step guide covering Survey Solutions Headquarters upload requirements, WKID: 102100 coordinate conventions, .tab preloading, and automated server upload & assignment creation using the SurveySolutionsAPIv2 R package, see vignette("survey-solutions-workflow", package = "vantorr").
